name: Breaker close-failure timer
summary: Detects that the requested close was not confirmed within the configured supervision interval.
description: Detects that the requested close was not confirmed within the configured supervision interval. A closing circuit combines an operator or automatic request with the conditions that allow the breaker to close. The closing coil releases stored mechanism energy where that construction is used; it is different from the spring-charging motor.

In a switchgear bus-coupler panel, a close request is checked against position, mechanism readiness and the selected live-bus or dead-bus conditions before the closing circuit is enabled. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Close request and feedback” at the input and “Failed-to-close alarm” at the output. The timer is not a breaker operating-time specification.

Follow request, permission and final coil output as separate signals. A permissive diagram must say which conditions block closing and what happens if a feedback signal becomes unavailable. The functional block is an independent explanation of this named application. Equipment-specific ratings, terminal connections and operating conditions must be established in the project documentation.
